        clc_312_100 + clc_313_100 + road1_100 + road2_100, data = umf, 
        keyfun = "halfnorm", output = "abund", mixture = "P", se = TRUE)

it will get computed (and converges), however I still get the warnings "In log(cp[J + 1]) : NaNs produced".

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] unmarked::gdistsamp(): error in optim: non-finite finite-difference value
parts:
hi Tomas,
 it is difficult to say exactly what your problem is here. However the models look to be very large, lots of parameters, and this usually causes a number of problems such as: parameters not being identifiable, bad starting values, or numerical instability due to sparse data and nearly confounded parameters. Or these in combination with other problems.
 
 The best thing to do is start building up your model from a very simple model with 0 or 1 covariates and make sure each model works well and then fit a more complex model.  Use the estimates from the previous model as starting values.
 
regards
andy
